title: Varmekartlegging og sårbarhet for hetebølger i Trondheim
description: 1. Generelt om oppdragetTrondheim kommune, heretter kalt oppdragsgiver, innbyr til åpen anbudskonkurranse i forbindelse med inngåelse av avtale på “Varmekartlegging og sårbarhet for hetebølger i Trondheim”. Konkurransen kunngjøres i DOFFIN, se www.doffin.no, gjennom oppdragsgiverens konkurransegjennomføringsverktøy (KGV) Mercell.2. BakgrunnTemperaturen i Norge har økt og vil fortsette å øke som følge av klimaendringene. Som følge av den generelle temperaturøkningen vil vi oftere oppleve perioder med ekstrem varme, såkalte “hetebølger”. En “norsk hetebølge” er definert som fem eller flere sammenhengende dager der maksimumtemperaturen er 27 grader eller høyere.Globalt har antallet hetebølger for perioden 2013-2022 økt med 94% sammenlignet med perioden 1986-2005. Også i Norge er det observert en markant økning i antallet hetebølger, samt en geografisk spredning av fenomenet, hvor hetebølger nå oppstår i områder hvor det tidligere har vært uvanlig.Urbane strøk er særlig utsatt for ekstrem varme på grunn av at bygningsmasse og harde overflater, som asfalt, både lagrer og reflekterer varme i nærområdet, noe som bidrar til å forsterke oppvarmingen. Forbrenning og varmetap fra trafikk og industri bidrar også til å øke temperaturen. Dette kalles “varmeøy-effekten”.Trær og annen vegetasjon spiller en viktig rolle for å regulere temperaturen lokalt. Grønne tak kan gi opp til 25 grader lavere temperatur på taket sammenlignet med konvensjonell takpapp. Tilsvarende kan gaterom og parker med vegetasjon gi en lokal temperatursenkning på inntil 10 grader. Med økende varmeproblematikk i urbane miljøer, blir grønnstruktur et viktig verktøy i arealplanlegginga for å redusere de negative effektene. Ekstrem varme bidrar til økt dødelighet og flere negative helsekonsekvenser. I perioden 2000-2019 ble det registrert 20 000 ekstra dødsfall per år, som følge av ekstrem varme i Europa. Hetebølger sammenfaller ofte med økt luftforurensing, noe som øker dødeligheten som følge av kardiovaskulære og respiratoriske sykdommer. I tillegg kan varmen gi dehydrering, heteslag, hodepine, dårlig søvn og redusert allmennstilstand. I Norge ble det påvist økt dødelighet under hetebølgen i 2025 , mens både Sverige og Finland registrerte økt dødelighet i forbindelse med hetebølgen i 2018.Noen befolkningsgrupper er særlig sårbare for ekstrem varme, f.eks. eldre, små barn og personer med underliggende sykdommer. I tillegg har lavinntektsgrupper, minoriteter, og leietakere som bor i gamle bygg lavere tilpasningsevne ved en hetebølge.Mange land og lokale myndigheter i Europa har utarbeidet rutiner og tiltaksplaner for å redusere de negative effektene av hetebølger. Forskning på tidligere hetebølger tyder på at byer, som har innført tilpasningstiltak og handlingsplaner for ekstrem varme, reduserer sammenhengen mellom hetebølger og negative helseeffekter. Det kan derfor antas at tilpasningstiltak er en effektiv måte for å redusere de negative konsekvensene. I Danmark oppgir en tredjedel av alle kommunene at de jobber med tilpasning til hetebølger, og i Sverige har over 80% av kommunene utarbeidet beredskapsplaner for høye temperaturer for sårbare grupper. I Norge har konsekvenser av hetebølger i liten grad blitt inkludert og håndtert i planverk og handlingsplaner, verken på nasjonalt, regionalt eller kommunalt nivå.

title: Felles EPJ for den offentlige tannhelsetjenesten
description: Konkurransen gjelder levering av en felles elektronisk pasientjournal (EPJ) for den offentlige tannhelsetjenesten, med integrasjon mot felles lagringsløsning. Løsningen leveres som en løpende tjeneste som inkluderer drift, utvikling og forvaltning. Anskaffelsens verdi anslås til over EØS terskelverdi. Volumet er et estimat og er ikke bindende for oppdragsgiver. For nærmere informasjon viser vi til anskaffelsesdokumentene. Et utkast til selve konkurransegrunnlaget er lagt ved dette kvalifiseringsgrunnlaget. Oppdragsgiver forbeholder seg retten til å foreta mindre, ikke vesentlige endringer i dette grunnlaget før leverandører inviteres til å gi tilbud. Oppdragsgiver tar forbehold om avlysning av konkurransen, blant annet i forbindelse med budsjettmessig dekning. Denne anskaffelsen er etter sin art vurdert til å ha en uvesentlig innvirkning på klima og miljø, jf. anskaffelsesloven § 5b tredje ledd. Begrunnelsen for dette er at anskaffelsen gjelder kjøp av en digital løsning for den offentlige tannhelsetjenesten der anskaffelsens art medfører at oppdragsgiver er avskåret fra å påvirke klima og miljøpåvirkningen, siden krav og kriterier som retter seg mot disse elementene ikke vil ha tilstrekkelig tilknytning til leveransen, jf. DFØs miljøveileder. Plikten til å stille krav om lærling er vurdert til å gjelde for denne anskaffelsen, jf. anskaffelsesloven § 5h. Se kontrakten for mer informasjon.

Technology Architect Level 3 The following SA Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: • Accenture Inc. • ADRM Technology Consulting Group Corp. • BoonBridge Corporation • CDW Canada Corp. • CGI Information Systems and Management Consultants Inc. • Cofomo Inc. • Deloitte Inc. • Donna Cona Inc., IBM Canada Limited Joint Venture • Flex Tech Services Inc • Primex Project Management Limited • Prologic Systems Ltd., and Maplesoft Consulting Inc. in JV • Skyfly Solutions Inc., iFathom Corp., EPI-Use Now Inc. in Joint Venture • Spaghetti Logic Inc. • TRM Technologies Inc. • Xelerance Corporation Description of Work: The objective of this requirement is to augment knowledge within the Department of Justice Canada’s (JUS) Cloud team to gather expertise and meet project requirements and specific AI initiatives. The required professional services will support the delivery of key infrastructure components, networking fixes and improvements as well as high visibility projects such as Otto , Artificial Intelligence and the Lakehouse. The Cloud Engineer will implement, configure, automate, and support cloud infrastructure, platform services, and cloud-native solutions in accordance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, enterprise architecture principles, and security controls. The Cloud Engineer will support the deployment, integration, modernization, and operational management of Microsoft Azure services, enterprise applications, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid cloud environments. The Cloud Architect will support cloud infrastructure, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, Azure platform services, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures. Responsibilities include the design of governance models, subscription hierarchies, landing zones, security architecture, integration patterns, DevSecOps practices, application hosting models, and reference architectures to support enterprise cloud adoption and integration with on-premises and cloud-based services. The Network Specialist will design, implement, document, and support cloud and hybrid networking solutions that provide secure, resilient, and high-performing connectivity between cloud, on-premises, partner, and externally hosted environments. The specialist will support enterprise cloud platforms, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures by designing and implementing networking services, secure integration patterns, and connectivity solutions. The Network Specialist will collaborate with Shared Services Canada (SSC), internal Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to design, implement, validate, and document network connectivity, firewall configurations, DNS services, certificate management, identity integration, private connectivity, and network security controls in accordance with Government of Canada standards and departmental policies. The Database Administrator will design, implement, maintain, and optimize database platforms across on-premises and Azure environments, ensuring the availability, performance, security, and recoverability of business-critical systems. The Database Administrator will implement and support backup, restore, high availability, disaster recovery, monitoring, and security controls, while providing technical advice and documentation related to database migrations, cloud integration, and operational best practices in coordination with application teams, Shared Services Canada (SSC), and internal security stakeholders. description: Psychological Risk Assessment Services (Psychologist) This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, for Joyceville Complex, Collins Bay Complex, Bath Complex, Millhaven Institution, Warkworth Institution, Beavercreek Complex, Grand Valley Complex, and the Regional Treatment Centre at Millhaven Institution and Bath Institution in the Ontario Region. Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) has a requirement to obtain professional psychological risk assessment services to support offender case management, decision-making, and risk management activities. Services include the completion of structured and unstructured psychological risk assessments, professional opinions, and related documentation in accordance with CSC policies, legislation, and professional standards of practice. Objectives: The objective of this requirement is to ensure CSC has timely access to qualified psychological expertise to conduct risk assessments that support safe, effective, and evidence-based correctional decision-making. Deliverables: The Contractor must provide professional psychological services, including but not limited to: • Completion of psychological risk assessments as requested by CSC; • Preparation of written psychological reports and professional opinions in the format required by CSC; • Documentation of findings in CSC-approved systems; • Participation in consultations or clarification discussions related to completed assessments, when required. Clarification discussions refer to consultations with CSC to explain, amend, or respond to questions related to completed psychological risk assessments. All deliverables must meet accepted professional standards, be delivered in English, and comply with CSC security, privacy, and operational requirements. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: Period of the Contract: The Work is to be performed during the period of January 16, 2027, to January 15, 2030. title: A.1. Application/Software Architect – Level 3
description: ISED is currently modernizing and maturing its end-to-end systems development lifecycle and project management lifecycle processes. The Application Software Architect – Level 3 will support the modernization, configuration, enhancement and ongoing evolution of the Clarity PPM platform throughout the two-year contract period. The resource will provide architecture, technical design, configuration, integration, analysis, documentation and technical advisory services in support of ISED's Clarity PPM environment. The resource will work under the direction of the Project Authority, who will establish priorities and assign work based on departmental requirements, the Clarity PPM roadmap and emerging business and technical needs. The resource will perform tasks including, but not limited to, the following: A. Architecture and Technical Design - Develop technical architectures, frameworks and strategies, either for an organization or for a major application area, to meet the business and application requirements. - Analyze functional requirements to identify information, procedures and decision flows. - Define input/output sources, including detailed plan for technical design phase, and obtain approval of the system proposal. - Advise on implementation paths, integration, interoperability and risk mitigation strategies relating to the implementation of Clarity PPM specific to the ISED Test and Production environments. B. Business Requirements Analysis - Elicit and analyze business requirements and related processes while adhering to relevant government policies and directives. C. Documentation and Standards - Evaluate existing procedures and methods, identify and document database content, structure, and application sub-systems, and develop data dictionary. - Define and document interfaces of manual to automated operations within application sub-systems, to external systems and between new and existing systems. - Identify and document system specific standards relating to programming, documentation and testing such as program libraries, data dictionaries, naming conventions. D. Clarity PPM Configuration and Advisory Services - Provide advice and hands-on services to architect and configure Clarity PPM in version 16.3x or more recent version. - Provide advice and hands-on expertise related to reporting requirements, including reporting to Treasury Board. - Provide advice and expertise on Government of Canada direction in Clarity PPM implementations. - Provide advice and expertise on private sector direction in Clarity PPM implementations.

title: W8703-270059 - Medium Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) RFP
description: Offer submissions must be submitted by 27 October 2026 by 14:00 EDT. The Defence Investment Agency, on behalf of the Department of National Defence, is soliciting bids for the acquisition of a Medium Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) capability. The requirement supports defence and security operations through the provision of deployable medium-range UAS capabilities for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, situational awareness, force protection, training, experimentation, and other operational requirements. The procurement includes the supply and delivery of a minimum of forty (40) UAS Systems, associated payloads, ground control stations, support equipment, technical publications, spare parts, software and firmware support, and train-the-trainer services. The requirement also includes airworthiness support, cybersecurity assurance, supply chain security, spectrum supportability, configuration management, and lifecycle sustainment requirements. This procurement is limited to qualified suppliers holding a Stream 1 Supply Arrangement under the Defence Drone Initiative (DDI).

title: W8703-270072 Request For Proposal Domestic UAS Bulk Purchase RFP
description: Offer submissions must be submitted by 27 October 2026 by 14:00 EDT. The Defence Investment Agency, on behalf of the Department of National Defence, is soliciting bids for the acquisition of a Domestic General Purpose Uncrewed Aircraft System (GPUAS) capability. The requirement supports domestic operations conducted by the Canadian Army, including intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance activities, situational awareness, force protection, disaster response, search and rescue support, infrastructure assessment, training, and experimentation. The procurement includes the supply and delivery of a minimum of eighty (80) UAS systems, associated payloads, ground control stations, support equipment, technical publications, spare parts, software and firmware support, train-the-trainer services and includes airworthiness support, cybersecurity assurance, supply chain security, spectrum supportability, configuration management, and lifecycle sustainment requirements. This procurement is limited to qualified suppliers holding a Stream 1 Supply Arrangement under the Defence Drone Initiative (DDI).

title: Senior Leader Cutterhead Dredge Forum
description: On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Senior Leader Cutterhead Dredge Forum will provide a platform for collaboration focused on challenges and opportunities in the cutterhead dredging industry. This forum is open to all cutterhead dredging companies that are currently performing business in the New Orleans District or are interested in doing so. The dredge forum will provide an opportunity for dredging industry leaders to meet with USACE senior leaders and technical personnel to discuss New Orleans District dredging projects and funding. There will be two (2) attendee slots (leadership positions) available per company. If your company is interested in attending, please complete one registration form for each company and submit no later than October 16, 2026. Should an attendee/company have a question they would like to be discussed at the forum, please submit the inquiries via email to Yojna Calix at Yojna.Calix@usace.army.mil and Ashley Wainright at Ashley.Wainright@usace.army.mil, no later than 25 September 2026. Time: 9:00am - 12:00pm (CST) Location: USACE New Orleans District Headquarters District Assembly Room (DARM) 7400 Leake Avenue New Orleans, LA 70118 This event is free of charge. All attendees will be required to Pre-register for the event for attendance and to gain access to the installation. Each company should submit one registration with both attendees� information. Furthermore, information about the company's cutterhead dredges, as well as dredging experience in the last three years, will be a part of the registration submittal and must be completed. TO REGISTER: Please register at: https://form.jotform.com/251965714470159 The acquisition forecast information does not represent a pre-solicitation notice or a Request for Quotation/Proposal and is not a commitment by the Government to purchase products or services. We look forward to meeting with you.

Tarkemmin hankinnan kohteena on asiantuntijapalvelu, jossa tehtävänä on laatia selvitys kompostitarkastusten nykytilasta sekä opas ja viestintämateriaalia kompostitarkastusten hyvistä käytännöistä. Hanke on tarkoitus toteuttaa yhteistyössä Suomen Kuntaliitto ry:n, kuntien jätehuoltoviranomaisten sekä tarvittavien muiden viranomaisten ja asiantuntijatahojen kanssa. Hankkeessa tulee lisäksi kuulla kotikompostointia harjoittavia asukkaita tarkoituksenmukaisella tavalla. Tiedonkeruussa voidaan hyödyntää esimerkiksi kyselyitä, haastatteluja ja työpajoja. Palveluntuottaja vastaa hankkeen suunnittelusta, toteutuksesta, sidosryhmäyhteistyöstä, aineiston analysoinnista, raportoinnista sekä hankkeessa tuotettavan oppaan ja muun viestintämateriaalin laatimisesta ja hankkeen tulosten esittelystä yleisö- ja sidosryhmätilaisuuksissa. Materiaali tuotetaan pääasiassa suomenkielisenä, mutta opas laaditaan myös ruotsiksi ja yleistajuinen viestintämateriaali myös ruotsiksi ja englanniksi. Ympäristöministeriö vastaa oppaan julkaisemisesta Ympäristöministeriön julkaisuja -sarjassa. Hankinnan kohteena oleva työ alkaa mahdollisimman pian hankintasopimuksen solmimisen jälkeen ja päättyy viimeistään 30.4.2027. Suomenkielisen oppaan ja viestintämateriaalien tulee olla valmiina viimeistään 31.3.2027. Valtakunnallinen info- tai verkkotilaisuus tulee toteuttaa viimeistään viikolla 14. Muiden tuotosten tulee olla valmiina tai toteutettuna viimeistään 30.4.2027. Tarjouksessa tulee esittää palvelun toteutuksesta vastaava asiantuntija (projektipäällikkö). Projektipäälliköllä tulee olla tukenaan palvelun toteutuksessa riittävä määrä muita asiantuntijoita. Hankintayksikkö on varannut toimeksiannon toteuttamiseen enintään 65 000 euroa (+mahdollinen alv). Hankinnan tarkempi kuvaus on liitteessä 1 (Palvelun kuvaus). Liitteessä 2 (CV-lomake) ilmoitetut hankinnan kohdetta koskevat vaatimukset ovat pakollisia vaatimuksia. Tarjottavan palvelun tulee täyttää kaikki palvelulle asetetut pakolliset vaatimukset, jotta sen voidaan katsoa olevan tarjouspyynnön mukainen. Hankintayksikkö valitsee yhden (1) toimittajan, jonka kanssa se tekee sopimuksen.,

title: Germany – Repair and maintenance services of security and defence materials – BG_1703_EU/26 - Werksinstandsetzung von Spiegel und Periskopbaugruppen des Systems GTK Boxer
description: Der Auftrag umfasst die Werksinstandsetzung von Spiegel und Periskopbaugruppen des Systems GTK Boxer. Die Bieter müssen im Rahmen der Angebotsabgabe berücksichtigen, dass die Angaben zu den jeweiligen Fachlosen lediglich aus den Vergangenheitswerten abgeleitete Schätzbedarfe sind sowie einen gegebenenfalls auftretenden Mehrbedarf (Sicherheitszuschlag) enthalten. Die tatsächlichen während der Vertragslaufzeit erfolgenden Beauftragungen können hinsichtlich der in einem Fachlos enthaltenen Bedarfsmengen der jeweiligen Versorgungsnummern abweichen. Die Obergrenze für den jeweiligen Auftrag bildet in jedem Fall die in dem betreffenden Fachlos zusammengefasste Gesamtmenge (Schätzbedarf + Sicherheitszuschlag). Eine Verpflichtung des AG, Einzelaufträge zu erteilen, wird durch diesen Vertrag nicht begründet. Die Vertragslaufzeit beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung und endet nach 4 Jahren. Wenn der bestehende Vertrag zwischen der HIL GmbH und der Bundeswehr, egal aus welchem Rechtsgrund endet, kann die Rahmenvereinbarung durch ein Sonderkündigungsrecht beendet werden.

title: France – Software package and information systems – FOURNITURE D’UNE SOLUTION DE FEEDBACK MANAGEMENT (ENQUETES DE SATISFACTION CLIENTS & NPS) ET PRESTATIONS ASSOCIEES
description: . Les directions des branches Services-Courrier-Colis (BSCC) et Grand Public et Numérique (BGPN) de La Poste, représentant six volets fonctionnels, souhaitent renouveler leur solution de Feedback Management et d'Écoute Client. L'objectif est de se doter d’une solution en mode SaaS pour l'administration et la gestion des enquêtes de satisfaction : - création de l'enquête, - programmation, - routage ... - jusque l'exploitation du verbatim, - la restitution des avis et résultats - et en dernier lieu la possibilité de donner une réponse personnalisée au destinataire de l’enquête. . La solution devra permettre la restitution des résultats à tous les maillons de l'organisation (Siège et Territoires), via une connexion SSO, avec des profils et rôles d’utilisateurs différents. . La solution devra permettre la création de dashboard en autonomie selon le type de profil. Les flux de données proviennent de plusieurs SI internes et externes à La Poste, selon les typologies d'enquêtes. . La solution SaaS devra donc s'interfacer avec d'autres outils de La Poste. Les enquêtes couvrent des prestations de services variées au sein de La Poste pour l'ensemble des Directions citées. Chaque Direction a des besoins spécifiques. . La solution devra se conformer au Règlement Général sur la Protection des Données (RGPD). . Le traitement des données personnelles de La Poste, y compris l’hébergement, la sauvegarde et/ou la consultation devra impérativement être localisé au sein de l'Union Européenne (UE), d’un pays de l’Espace Economique Européen (EEE), d’un pays reconnu comme adéquat par l’Union Européenne.. La solution devra également respecter la Politique de Sécurité des SI du Groupe La Poste (PSSIG).

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE High-Performance Computing Software Development and Technical Services REQUIREMENTS-25-1463-27 This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal or Quotation. It is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract nor will the Government pay for any information provided; no basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result from a response to this Sources Sought Notice or Government use of any information provided. Pursuant to FAR Part 10 (Market Research), the purpose of this notice is to: Determine if sources capable of satisfying the agency's requirements exist. Determine whether the acquisition should utilize any of the small business programs in accordance with FAR Part 19. Pursuant to FAR Part 6 and FAR Part 19, competition and set-aside decisions may be based on the results of this market research. This notice in no way obligates the Government to any further action. Requirement: This notice is issued by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Western Acquisition Division (WAD) and Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory (GFDL) to identify sources capable of providing the following: The GFDL, located on Princeton University's Forrestal Campus, Princeton, NJ, is a NOAA research laboratory in the Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research (OAR). GFDL�s mission is to be a world leader in the development of comprehensive, integrated and unified models of the Earth system comprising the atmosphere, oceans, land, biosphere, cryosphere, and ecosystems; and application of these models for the seamless understanding, predictions and projections of the Earth system, from hours to decades and from global-to-regional spatial scales, accounting for natural variations and forced changes. This procurement is to obtain High-Performance Computing (HPC) software development and technical support services for the GFDL. This support is essential to ensuring that users are provided with the necessary support for the systems, network, and software needed to continue to advance the GFDL and NOAA mission. This effort does not include procuring IT equipment or software, per se, though contract personnel may help define requirements for equipment, software, and services to be acquired by the Government The Statement of Objectives, Performance Work Statements and other supporting documents outline the primary performance-based tasks required to successfully satisfy the need in Management Support Services, Technical Support Services, and Scientific Support Services. The scope of this effort shall encompass all of the task areas described in the Performance Work Statements. The period of performance is anticipated to be a one-year base ordering period, with four additional one-year optional ordering periods. NAICS Code/Size Standard: The applicable NAICS Code is 541511, Custom Computer Programming Services, and the size standard is $34.0M. title: Renovate Building 736 Fort Leonard Wood, MO
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District (USACE) is seeking contractors to renovate Building 736 at Fort Leonard Wood, MO. Building 736 is a 40,640 Square Foot (SF), three story, permanent construction barrack facility was built in the 1960s and currently houses basic training/one station unit training (BT/OSUT) trainees. A design was completed by the Kansas City District Corps of Engineers in April 2019 and updated in accordance with UFC changes in June of 2024. This requirement will consist of selective demolition and renovation and modernization of one barracks building and associated sitework at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri. This project includes renovation of a 40,640 SF Barracks Building and construction of an addition of approximately 3,000 SF addition to the building, and associate fine grading, landscaping, and other site work per the plans and specifications provided.

This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which small business contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified small business contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS 339999 - All Other Miscellaneous Manufacturing and PSC 7690 - Miscellaneous Printed Matter Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) USPTO is seeking a contractor who can fulfill the agency�s requirements for the following awards, certificates, medallions, as well as appropriate packaging and direct shipping for each. This requirement includes manufacturing, assembly and preparing the awards for delivery and shipping directly to the recipient or to an agency office as required. The Office of Human Resource (OHR) supports a variety of non-monetary awards to recognize and reward employee excellence. Superior performance is generally considered as the type of employee performance that contributes, directly or indirectly, to the mission of the USPTO. These non-monetary awards include Bronze Medal Awards, Career Achievement Awards which includes Distinguished Career Awards and Exceptional Career Awards, Retirement Certificates, Directors Award, Length of Service Award and Leadership in Action Award. These awards range in style and type to include framed certificates, medals encased in leucite and presented with a certificate and display box and laser etched clear crystal desktop awards. Note: Sample photos of the awards are attached in a pdf to this RFI 1) Bronze Medal Awards- This award is used to recognize an organization, group or individual employees who have made a major impact on the effectiveness of the USPTO. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity per year is up to 450. 2) Distinguished Career Awards: This award marks at least 20 years of superior performance as an employee of the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 150. 3) Exceptional Career Awards: This award marks at least ten (10) years of superior performance with the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 275. 4) Retirement Certificates: The purpose of this certificate is to recognize USPTO employees upon the occasion of their retirement. These are ordered/requested upon notification of an employee retiring. Framed certificates are created throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 120. 5) Directors Award: The purpose of this award is to recognize individuals and/or group recognition for contributions to the Agency, Managers, supervisors or other employees may nominate those whose contributions have far exceeded expectations or reflect positively on the USPTO. These awards are sporadic throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 100. 6) Leadership in Action Award. The recipients are recognized during the USPTO Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony. The Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity of Leadership in Action awards is up to 400 per year. The three (3) award tiers are Supervisor of the Year (SOTY), Supervisor of the Year (SOTY) Finalist, Approved Nominated Supervisors. Each award tier has a different associated cost and quantity. 7) Length of Service Award: The purpose of this award is to recognized USPTO employee�s length of Federal service. This award is issued monthly. The estimated quantity per year is approximately 2,600. The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the experience and the range of awards and services provided. This will allow USPTO management to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command (ACC) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as market research to identify qualified Original Component Manufacturers (OCMs) and their Tier-1 direct distributors (directly working with manufacturer) capable of supplying commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS), industrial, and defense-grade microelectronics in sustained, large-scale production volumes for Circuit Card Assembly (CCA) integration. title: LOC Novel High-Density Optical Data Storage
description: The Library of Congress, hereinafter referred to as the �Library� or �LOC�,� is exploring innovative preservation methods for its digital collections. The LOC is seeking to determine the feasibility of utilizing ultra-high density optical data storage designed for the long-term preservation of a subset of the Library�s digital collections. Currently, the Library manages over 1 billion unique objects of digital preservation data (~33 petabytes) via traditional storage methods. For longevity and reduced migration intervals, it may be reasonable for this portion of data to be permanently stored on a novel medium. The focus would be on a solution that exhibits high areal density, a long lifespan, reduced maintenance/migration cycles, is immutable, and displays a high level of durability. The Library aims to demonstrate the feasibility of an innovative optical data storage solution as a high-density, scalable, and durable medium for storing its preservation collection. The Library wishes to examine the feasibility of this method on a small subset of its digital collections. To be successful, a variety of data formats�including video, audio, text, and images� must be encoded onto the media, errors must be detected/recorded, preservation techniques must be validated and select data must be recalled/read with high fidelity. This work will contribute to the boundary pushing field of high-density optical data storage while pushing the boundaries of access and preservation. The desired outcomes of this requirement are as follows: The successful writing of 1TB of the Library�s digital data in various formats (video, audio, images, text) onto a robust high-density optical media designed to outlast legacy storage solutions at a higher areal density. The determination of the accuracy of the writing process by demonstrating early-stage error detection and ultimate 100% recovery of data. The documentation of successful processes, shortcomings, error rates, timelines, potential solutions to issues, risks, trends, and technological improvements throughout the period of performance as they pertain to the media of choice. Proof of concept for the potential indefinite storage approach of the Library�s data on a novel optical storage medium. The successful recall and reading of all Library-furnished digital files that have been encoded on the media of choice. The isolation of a subset of the data will be carefully curated and stored for the purposes of an educational and artistic display. This will used for educational and display purposes for Library visitors.

title: Architect & Engineering Services, Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award (A&E) Contracts needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs required by Federal Prison Industries (FPI)
description: The Federal Prison Industries (FPI) intends to solicit and award a competitively negotiated Architect and Engineer (A&E) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Contract needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs. The Architect and Engineer (A&E) shall furnish professional architectural, engineering, and related technical services, as specified herein, to the United States Government, Department of Justice, Federal Prison Industries (FPI). The resulting contracts will consist of a one?year base period and will include options for four additional one?year periods. All work performed under this contract shall pertain to projects located at FPI facilities within the contiguous United States. Pursuant to the terms of this contract, the A&E may be required to perform services under the following major categories, including other closely related services as necessary: � Review design and construction documents prepared by other A&E firms or by FPI personnel. � Prepare, develop, and produce design and construction documents for new facility construction, facility additions, and renovation or modernization of existing facilities. � Develop detailed and accurate cost estimates for construction activities, renovations, contract modifications, and claims. � Conduct Value Engineering (V/E) analyses and perform additional cost evaluation studies, as required. � Develop, maintain, and update project schedules and construction schedules. � Provide assistance in preventing, mitigating, and resolving disputes or claims arising from design or construction activities. � Furnish comprehensive architectural and engineering services encompassing all disciplines necessary to ensure the successful execution and completion of assigned projects. � Provide, as required, studies; design development; construction documents; technical specifications; support during bid negotiation; construction administration; and project closeout services. � Develop procedures, prepare construction documents and work statements, support master planning efforts, conduct regulatory compliance evaluations, and assist in the preparation of design?build documentation. � Prepare construction specifications that uphold the principles of full and open competition. � Comply with all general requirements applicable to task orders issued under this contract. In accordance with the Brooks Architect-Engineer Act, award(s) shall be made to the successful firm(s) based on demonstrated competence and qualifications to perform the services at fair and reasonable prices. Prior to this solicitation issuance, technical evaluations were conducted. This solicitation was then issued to the most highly rated firm(s). Therefore, in response to the solicitation, consideration for a contract award will be based solely upon the hourly rates, overhead and profit that are proposed and found to be fair and reasonable. Offerors are advised that award maybe made without discussions. Therefore, the initial proposal should provide sufficient information to recommend award without discussions and should reflect the offeror�s ability to perform at a reasonable price.

title: Solicitation - Residential Reentry Services and Home Confinement Services within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island.
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC26R00000009 Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services and Home Confinement (HC) services for male and female offenders located within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island. Home Confinement radius is within 100 miles of the RRC facility. The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which are located within city limits of Pawtucket, Rhode Island. Home Confinement radius is within 100 miles of the RRC facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. title: Grand Island Mitigation Site
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Project Description: Grand Island Mitigation Project Anticipated Posting Date: 09 October 2026 Sources Sought Number: W9123827X1CQX SAM Posting Title: USACE SPK DBB Construction � Grand Island Mitigation Project � Sacramento, California SAM Posting Description: This Sources Sought Notice is being issued for market research purposes to determine the availability, capability, and interest of small business firms for a potential Government requirement. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE; requests for a solicitation will go unanswered. No award will be made from this Notice. Responses will be used to determine potential acquisition strategies, understand current market capabilities, and to gain knowledge of potential sources. GENERAL SCOPE: The Sacramento River Grand Island Mitigation Project is a restoration initiative on a 233-acre site located at the western tip of Grand Island in Sacramento County, California, situated at the confluence of the Sacramento River, Steamboat Slough, and Cache Slough. The project is designed to create and enhance approximately 84 acres of self-sustaining aquatic and riparian habitat as compensatory mitigation for the American River Common Features (ARCF) project. The construction scope entails approximately 108,000 cubic yards of total excavation to establish a tidal channel network and create an interior "habitat bowl" with islands and peninsulas, alongside breaching an existing berm to connect the site to Steamboat Slough. Excavated material will be utilized to construct on-site features such as the islands and peninsulas, while the remaining excess material will initially be placed in designated uncompacted fill areas on the island and, if settlement issues arise, hauled off-site by barge. To support the federally listed Western, Yellow-Billed Cuckoo, the revegetation plan establishes a continuous riparian corridor by planting water-tolerant trees and shrubs at lower elevations, transitioning to diverse, later-successional trees and native grasses at higher elevations. Project features also include protecting the Valley Elderberry Longhorn Beetle by transplanting impacted elderberry shrubs to designated on-site areas, followed by irrigation and maintenance of these transplants for the duration of this contract. To stabilize the breach, the design utilizes a hybrid bioengineered approach featuring a quarry stone riprap toe from the channel inverted up to 4 feet, transitioning to a bioengineered slope reinforced with erosion control fabrics and live willow cuttings above. Construction scheduling is subject to strict environmental windows, requiring all in-water work (such as activities in Steamboat Slough) to occur strictly between July 1st and October 31st. To isolate the breach work area from the active waterway during in-water construction, a temporary 250-foot-long steel sheet pile cofferdam must be installed and then fully removed upon project completion. The potential requirement may result in a firm-fixed-price solicitation issued approximately late November 2026. If solicited, the Government intends to award the anticipated requirement by mid-March 2027. The Government estimates that construction of the potential requirement can be completed within six hundred and sixty-five (665) calendar days from receipt of Notice to Proceed. If market conditions indicate this estimate may be unrealistic, respondents are encouraged to provide specific information (such as known equipment lead times or other timeline concerns) for Government consideration when responding to this Sources Sought Notice. The Government currently estimates the magnitude of construction for the potential project is between $15,000,000 and $20,000,000. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for the potential requirement is anticipated to be 562910, Remediation Services. The small business size standard for the NAICS, as established by the U.S. Small Business Administration, is $25,500,000 annual revenue. The Product Service Code for the potential requirement is anticipated to be Y1KZ, Construction of Other Conservation and Development Facilities. If there is a reasonable expectation that at least two (2) responsible small business concerns under this NAICS can provide the anticipated services at fair market prices, the Contracting Officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. If competition is set-aside for small businesses, Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, requires that the Prime Contractor will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. If no set aside is made, the requirement is competed with full and open competition, and the awarded Contractor is not a small business, the Contractor will be required to self-perform the percent of work identified in the solicitation under FAR 52.236-1, Performance of Work by the Contractor. Contractors with the skill, capabilities, workload capacity, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the project described above (either through self-performance and/or Subcontractor management) are invited to provide capability statements to the primary point of contact listed below. Other than small businesses are also encouraged to submit Capability Statements. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Responses must be limited to ten (10) 8.5 x 11 inch pages with a minimum font size of point 10. Please provide the following information: 1) Company name, System for Award Management Unique Entity Identification number (SAM UEID) or Employer Identification Number (EIN), address, point of contact name, contact phone number, contact e-mail address, and statement identifying whether the company employs union or non-union workers. 2) Experience and capability to complete contracts of similar magnitude and complexity to the potential requirement, including at least three (3) examples of comparable work performed within the past six (6) years. Each example should include a brief description of the project, description of the work performed (identification of self-performance and/or Subcontractor management), customer name, customer satisfaction, timeliness of performance, dollar value of the project, and whether there were any challenges experienced during the project (delays, investigations, health and safety issues, labor shortages, management/organizational issues, etc.). 3) Business size and socioeconomic type for the applicable NAICS (ex: Woman-Owned Small Business, Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), certified Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), 8(a) Participant, small business, or other than small business (large business)). 4) Bonding capability (in the form of a Surety letter). Please submit all capabilities statements, information, brochures, and/or marketing material as one (1) document, limited to the page maximum above. Responses will not be considered an offer, proposal, or bid for any solicitation that may result from this Notice. Moreover, responses will not restrict the Government to an acquisition approach. This Notice is for information and planning purposes only. Respondents will not be notified of the results of any review conducted or the capability statements received. Please provide responses and/or questions by e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Jessica Padilla, at Jessica.Padilla@usace.army.mil by 1100 / 11:00 a.m. (PT) Tuesday, 27 October 2026. Please include the Sources Sought Notice number, �W9123827X1CQX�, in the e-mail subject line.

title: Shipboard Air Conditioning Plant System Sustainment Plan (SSP)
description: 1.0 PURPOSE AND BACKGROUND PAE Maritime is conducting market research to identify responsible sources capable of providing some or all the sustainment capabilities required to support U.S. Navy surface-ship centrifugal, reciprocating, and rotary air conditioning (AC) plants worldwide. The information received will help the Government assess available industry capabilities and determine an appropriate acquisition strategy, contract structure, and number of sources. The Navy�s AC Plant System Sustainment Plan (SSP) establishes a standardized, scalable approach intended to improve materiel condition and operational availability across multiple AC plant configurations, ship classes, and geographically dispersed maintenance activities. The contemplated scope includes maintenance, technical expertise, materiel, rotable inventory management, engineering, logistics, training, and emergent field services. The Government is considering a range of acquisition approaches, which may include a single-award Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract, multiple contracts, or coordinated capabilities from multiple sources. No final acquisition strategy has been selected. Respondents may describe capabilities they can provide individually, through existing or proposed teaming arrangements, or as part of a broader sustainment solution. 2.0 CONTEMPLATED SUSTAINMENT CAPABILITIES The Government is seeking information on the capabilities summarized below and detailed in the Capability Certification Matrix (Table 1). Respondents may address any one or more capability areas. For each area addressed, identify current capabilities, how the work would be performed, and any relevant limitations, dependencies, or capability-development needs. 2.1 Major AC Plant Pit Stops Major Pit Stops include comprehensive plant assessment, troubleshooting, corrective maintenance, component repair or replacement, in-place compressor overhaul, testing, and restoration of the plant to operational condition. Major Pit Stops must be completed within a mandatory maintenance window of six weeks or less. Respondents should identify relevant experience, available personnel and facilities, configuration coverage, and demonstrated ability to meet this schedule. 2.2 Embedded AC&R Technical Expertise at SIMAs The Government is considering embedded air conditioning and refrigeration (AC&R) expertise at designated Navy Shore Intermediate Maintenance Activities (SIMAs) to support Sailor training and Navy-led Minor Pit Stops. Support may include hands-on instruction, troubleshooting, maintenance planning, and technical oversight. Minor Pit Stops must also be completed within a mandatory maintenance window of six weeks or less. 2.3 AC Plant Materiel Support This capability includes identifying, sourcing, procuring, managing, and delivering configuration-specific repair parts, components, assemblies, and overhaul materiel for planned maintenance, emergent repairs, casualty response, and restoration of AC plant capability. 2.4 Global Warehouse and Rotable Pool Management This capability includes establishing and managing rotable inventories and Overhaul Parts Packages (OPPs), including storage, configuration control, issue and return, repair or overhaul, replenishment, transportation, and positioning inventory to support geographically dispersed maintenance activities. 2.5 Engineering, Technical Data, Logistics, and Integrated Product Support This capability may include configuration-specific engineering and technical assistance, technical data and documentation, maintenance procedures, failure and root-cause analysis, technical dispositions, reliability and maintainability support, obsolescence management, and other Integrated Product Support. 2.6 Global Unplanned and Emergent Field Services This capability includes responsive technical troubleshooting, on-site assessment, engineering assistance, repair recommendations, identification and sourcing of required materiel, and other field services needed to restore AC plant capability at Navy locations worldwide. Respondents should describe geographic coverage, response capability, and the ability to support emergent work while meeting scheduled maintenance commitments. 3.0 CAPABILITY CERTIFICATION MATRIX AND SUPPORTING EVIDENCE Respondents should complete Table 1 for each capability area addressed. For each area, select YES, PARTIAL, or NO and identify the proposed method of performance: organic capability, existing OEM or license arrangement, subcontractor or teaming partner, or capability to be developed. A response of YES should reflect current capability. PARTIAL should identify the elements currently available and any gaps. NO indicates that the respondent does not currently possess the capability. Respondents may identify capabilities available through subcontractors, teaming partners, suppliers, license agreements, or other third-party arrangements. Clearly identify the organization responsible for each capability and whether the relationship is established or would need to be formed. Distinguish current capabilities from those that would require additional agreements, licensing, qualification, investment, or development. Provide concise, specific, and verifiable supporting information for each YES or PARTIAL response, as applicable. Useful evidence may include: Relevant contracts or programs, customers, periods of performance, and scope of work; AC plant configurations or comparable equipment supported and geographic locations served; Personnel, facilities, tooling, diagnostic or test equipment, inventory, and logistics infrastructure; Demonstrated maintenance capacity, schedule performance, response times, and relevant past performance; and Access to technical data, licenses, specialized resources, or other arrangements necessary to perform the work, including any material limitations. Respondents are not expected to provide a detailed technical proposal or develop a new solution in response to this notice. Concise evidence sufficient to describe the respondent�s capabilities and approach is encouraged. 4.0 ALTERNATIVE APPROACHES AND CAPABILITY GAPS Respondents may identify alternative approaches that could meet the Government�s underlying sustainment needs or improve maintenance execution, materiel availability, technical support, reliability, maintainability, or operational availability. Briefly describe the approach, the requirements it addresses, any differences from the contemplated approach, and any Government resources, approvals, or changes that would be necessary. The Government makes no commitment to adopting a proposed alternative. Respondents should identify any capability gaps, dependencies, or limitations that could affect performance, including the anticipated time and conditions needed to establish a capability. The Government may use this information to assess individual capabilities, combinations of capabilities, teaming approaches, and the feasibility of different acquisition structures. 5.0 RESPONSE FORMAT Responses should not exceed ten pages, excluding Table 1 and relevant supporting documentation. Respondents need only address the capability areas relevant to their organization and proposed approach. Please include: Company name and address, UEI, CAGE code, and business size/status; Primary point of contact, including email and telephone number; Completed Capability Certification Matrix (Table 1); A concise description of the capability areas addressed and the proposed method of performance; Specific supporting evidence for each YES or PARTIAL response, including relevant past performance where available; and Identification of any relevant teaming, subcontracting, licensing, technical-data access, or other third-party arrangements and their status. title: COVER, ACCESS, AIRCRAFT / NSN 1560-01-686-8294 / FA-18 AIRCRAFT
description: A 100% Small Business Set-Aside solicitation will be issued to establish an Indefinite Quantity Contract (IQC) for NSN 1560-01-686-8294, a COVER, ACCESS, AIRCRAFT. The award will be for a 5-year base period. The Estimated Annual Quantity (EAQ) is 40 each. Production units will be FOB: Destination; Inspection /Acceptance: Destination. Item is not critical, nor deemed a Critical Safety Item. Export Control applies. Surge does not apply. The proposed contract action is for supplies for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one or a limited number of sources under the authority of FAR 6.302. The NSN is in accordance with BASIC DRAWING # 76301 74A802662, Revision E, DTD 05/24/2005, PPN 74A802662-1001. DLA Aviation does possess complete technical data on this part for any interested vendor. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all proposals received within forty-five days after date of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Based upon market research, the Government is not using the policies contained in Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, in its solicitation for the described supplies. However, interested persons may identify to the contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item within 15 days of this notice. This solicitation may include Procurement Note L09, Reverse Auction. Since a reverse auction may be conducted, offerors are encouraged to access the Procurex system and review the reverse auction help tutorials at https//dla.procurexinc.com to learn more about how to participate in an auction. In order to receive an award, regardless of dollar value, contractors must be registered in the System For Award Management (sam.gov). The final contract award decision may be based upon a combination of price, past performance and other evaluation factors as described in the solicitation. The estimated solicitation issue date is 09/25/2026 and is when technical data will become available via cFolders on DIBBS. A copy of the solicitation will be available via DIBBS at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ on the issue date cited in the RFP. Choose the RFP you wish to download. RFPs are in portable document format (PDF). To download and view these documents you will need the latest version of Adobe Acrobat Reader. This software is available free at http://www.adobe.com. A paper copy of this solicitation will not be available to requesters.

title: Boat Tow
description: The MCIEast Cherry Point Satellite Contracting Office aboard MCAS Cherry Point, NC has a requirement to obtain Professional Services to have a decommissioned vessel towed from the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard to Brandt Island Shoal, Pamlico Sound, NC, as required by Range Management aboard Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point NC. The proposed action is considered as a Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Set-aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 488330. Any questions received after the stated deadline will not be addressed.

title: Robotic Sheet Metal Forming CAPABILITY REQUEST FOR INFORMATION
description: This is a Capability Request for Information (CRFI) issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) and does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with responding to this notice. The United States Air Force Rapid Sustainment Office (RSO) is conducting market research analysis to identify existing solutions for an on-demand, dieless robotic sheet metal forming capability. This capability is intended to produce structural components, brackets, panels, skin sections, and spare parts for support equipment, and aircraft at depot, maintenance, or factory-level facilities. Traditional manufacturing of sheet metal parts relies on heavy, expensive tooling, dies, and presses that require long lead times, high upfront costs, and physical storage. Robotic sheet metal forming�utilizing dual-sided or single-sided synchronized robotic arm manipulators equipped with generic, interchangeable forming styli�offers a flexible, software-defined alternative. The objective of this research is to identify commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) or rapidly adaptable solutions capable of being integrated into standard industrial manufacturing and maintenance facilities. This capability is aimed at reducing reliance on traditional supply chains, eliminating the need for part-specific hard tooling, and dramatically accelerating low-volume manufacturing and prototyping cycles. Submitters are encouraged to highlight existing commercial technologies and details on how their hardware and software solutions can be integrated into industrial DoW facilities. Submitters may also identify optional services, such as operator training, technical support, tooling/stylus consumables, and system maintenance. See the attachment with this notice for additional details.

title: E21 PRCA HVAC REPLACEMENT
description: Planet Ranch Conservation Area HVAC Replacement The Bureau of Reclamation (Reclamation), Lower Colorado Basin, Multi-Species Conservation Program (MSCP), has a requirement to replace two existing HVAC systems on two bunk houses at Planet Ranch Conservation Area (PRCA). PRCA is located in a remote area outside of Parker, Arizona along the Bill Williams River. Access to the site is via an unpaved, sometimes primitive road that may be affected by weather and local conditions. Contractors should plan accordingly for transportation of personnel, materials, and equipment. Building 1 is approximately 3,000 square feet and Building 2 is approximately 2,400 square feet. Both buildings are single story houses. To support onsite work, contractors will have the option to stay in the existing bunk houses for the duration of the HVAC replacement activities. Government-furnished heavy equipment, including a telehandler, will be available onsite for use in removing the two existing HVAC units from the roof. This equipment may be used by the contractor in accordance with Reclamation's standards for government-furnished property. This requirement is 100% set-aside for small businesses. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 238220, Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors with a corresponding small business size standard of $19M. The magnitude of this construction project is between $100,000.00 and $200,000.00. This requirement will be solicited and awarded using the methods outlined in FAR Part 36, Construction Contracts, and FAR Part 13, Simplified Acquisitions. The Government contemplated award of one firm-fixed price purchase order. Quoters are expected to download all attachments and read thoroughly in order to provide the required information with quote submittal. title: NATO Business Opportunity: Audio Visual Lifecycle Services (AVLS)
description: The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) intends to issue a solicitation for the provision of Audio Visual Lifecycle Services (AVLS) at Camp Casteau (SHAPE). Potential U.S. prime contractors must 1) maintain a professionally active facility (office, factory, laboratory, etc.) within the United States, 2) hold a Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the level of SECRET or higher, 3) be pre-approved for participation in NATO Competitive Procurement (NCP), 4) be issued a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) by the Department of Commerce (DOC), and 5) register with NCIA�s eProcurement tool, Neo: https://www.ncia.nato.int/business/procurement/neo-eprocurement The reference for the solicitation is CO-424399-AVLS and all correspondence concerning the solicitation should include this reference. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The purpose of this contract is to establish a multi-year framework for the technical support, maintenance, configuration management, training, and operational assistance of designated audiovisual and visualization systems located at Camp Casteau. The contract encompasses the following system families: Video Conference Systems, Video Wall Systems, Digital Signage Systems, Large Display Systems, and Public Address (PA) Systems. BECOMING ELIGIBLE TO BID NCP requires that the U.S. Government issue a DOE for potential U.S. prime contractors interested in this project. Before the U.S. Government can do so, however, the U.S. Government must approve the U.S. firm for participation in NCP. U.S. firms are approved for NCP on a facility-by-facility basis. The U.S. NCP application is a one-time application. The application requires supporting documentation in the form of 1) a company resume or capability statement indicating contracts completed as a prime contractor and 2) an annual report or set of financial documents indicating compilation, review, or audit by an independent CPA. The U.S. Government continues to accept the legacy NATO International Competitive Bidding (ICB) application for participation in NCP. U.S. firms can download a copy of the legacy ICB application from the following website: https://www.bis.gov/about-bis/bis-leadership-and-offices/SIES/business-opportunities-nato DOC is the U.S. Government agency that approves NCP applications. title: Denmark – Management-related services – Kontrakt om drift af Banedanmarks svellefabrik
description: Banedanmark ønsker at indgå en kontrakt med en driftsleverandør, som kan forestå den daglige, løbende drift af Banedanmarks svellefabrik beliggende Vejlbyvej 1, 7000 Fredericia og således ved brug af svellefabrikkens produktionsapparat producere og levere betonsveller i form af strækningssveller og sporskiftesveller, herunder svelletyper til særlige sporkonstruktioner såsom skinneudtræk ved broer, i forspændt beton til brug for Banedanmarks varetagelse af opgaven som jernbaneinfrastrukturforvalter. Produktionen sker efter long line-metoden. Driftsleverandøren skal i forbindelse hermed blandt andet: - Forestå en rationel og økonomisk forsvarlig produktion og levering af betonsveller af typerne Strækningssveller og Sporskiftesveller i overensstemmelse med kontraktens vilkår, - Som minimum opfylde kravene i DS/EN ISO 9001:2015 eller en tilsvarende standard for kvalitetsledelsessystem, jf. bilag 5 - Forestå kvalitetssikring af svelleproduktionen, - Løbende samarbejde med Banedanmark om en tilrettelæggelse af driften af Svellefabrikken, herunder deltage i samarbejdsmøder, - For egen regning indkøbe de nødvendige råvarer og materialer, der indgår i produktionen, i det omfang disse ikke i henhold til kontrakten er bygherreleverancer, som Banedanmark leverer, - Stille den nødvendige tekniske og administrative ekspertise til rådighed for driften af Svellefabrikken, herunder rådgive Banedanmark om udvikling og tilpasning af produktionen, - Bistå Banedanmark i forbindelse med ændringer af Svellefabrikken, herunder omstilling af produktionsapparatet med henblik på produktion af andre svelletyper, - Medvirke til en hensigtsmæssig tilrettelæggelse og gennemførelse af afhentningen af sveller fra fabrikken, herunder forestå læsning af sveller i forbindelse med transport af færdigproducerede sveller fra Svellefabrikken. For information om den historiske produktion af sveller henvises til bilag 17 til kontrakten. Driftsleverandøren forventes at overtage ansvaret for driften af svellefabrikken den 1.1.2028. Perioden fra den 1.9.2027 og forventeligt frem til den 31.1.2028 betragtes som en etableringsperiode. I denne periode samarbejder parterne tæt om hurtigst muligt at få etableret grundlaget for en stabil og effektiv drift af Svellefabrikken i overensstemmelse med kontraktens vilkår. Der henvises i øvrigt til Bilag 6, tidsplan for etablering. Den daglige ledelse af Svellefabrikken skal forestås af en fabrikschef. Fabrikschefen skal være ansat hos Driftsleverandøren (Banedanmarks kontraktpart). Kommunikationen mellem den af Driftsleverandøren antagne fabrikschef og Banedanmark skal foregå på dansk. Kontrakten er ikke til hinder for, at Banedanmark kan indkøbe sveller af tredjemand. Banedanmark er berettiget til at videresælge sveller til tredjemand. Lovbekendtgørelse nr. 710 af 20.8.2002 om lønmodtageres retsstilling ved virksomhedsoverdragelse med senere ændringer (Virksomhedsoverdragelsesloven) finder anvendelse i forbindelse med Driftsleverandørens overtagelse af ansvaret for driften af Svellefabrikken. De nærmere oplysninger herom fremgår af udbudsmaterialet. Ansøgere, som bliver prækvalificeret, vil have mulighed for at deltage i 2 fremvisninger af svellefabrikken. De konkrete datoer fremgår af tidsplanen i punkt 3 i udbudsbetingelserne.

Für die Nutzung der Stellplätze wird eine straßenrechtliche Sondernutzungserlaubnis für die Dauer von 6 Jahren erteilt. Die Stellplätze werden im Rahmen eines einheitlichen Auswahlverfahrens an einen Carsharing-Anbieter vergeben. Der Carsharing-Anbieter ist verpflichtet, auf allen 25 Stellplätzen dauerhaft ein Carsharing-Angebot während der gesamten Laufzeit der straßenrechtlichen Sondernutzungserlaubnis zu betreiben. Dabei agiert der Carsharing-Anbieter wirtschaftlich selbstständig. Er trägt das wirtschaftliche Risiko der Unternehmung und leistet die Administration und Disposition. Er trägt die Verantwortung für ein wirksames Marketing des Carsharing-Angebotes. Die Abrechnung des Carsharing-Angebots hat exakt, anhand der tatsächlichen gebuchten Zeitintervalle und der gefahrenen Kilometer, zu erfolgen. Das Carsharing hat ausschließlich stationsbasiert zu erfolgen - es ist kein free-floating oder stationsflexibler Betrieb zulässig.

description: Rahmenvereinbarung Kanalreinigung- und Inspektion für Einrichtungen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland in Schleswig-Holstein. _________________________________________________________________________________________________ Im Zuge von Bestandsaufnahmen zur Erstellung von LAKs (Liegenschaftsbezogenen Abwasserentsorgungskonzepten), Gewährleistungsabnahmen von Kanalsanierungsmaßnahmen, Kanalinspektionen vor Kanalsanierungsmaßnahmen, sowie Abnahmeinspektionen von Kanalsanierungsmaßnahmen sollen Schmutz- und / oder Regenwasserkanalisationen von Liegenschaften des Bundes vollständig und/oder teilweise gereinigt und auf Schäden untersucht werden. Die entsprechenden Liegenschaften können der beigefügten Liste entnommen werden. Es handelt sich um Liegenschaften mit weniger als 100 m Kanallänge bis zu mehreren Kilometern Kanalnetz. _________________________________________________________________________________________________ Hinweis: Beschränkung der Zahl der Lose, für die ein Bieter den Zuschlag erhalten kann. Die Abgabe eines Angebotes für mehrere Lose ist zulässig. Es wird allerdings pro Auftragnehmer maximal 1 Los beauftragt, da der Umfang der Arbeiten sehr umfangreich ist. Jeder Bieter kann Wünsche in Form einer Liste äußern, welches Los er vordringlich gewinnen möchte, sollte er der Bestbietende in mehreren Losen sein. Er erhält dann das Los, das in seiner persönlichen Liste auf Rang 1 ist. Fehlt diese Liste steht es der Vergabestelle frei das zu gewinnende Los festzusetzen. D. h. Im ersten Schritt wird geprüft, welcher Bieter welches Los gewinnt. Sollte jeder Bieter jeweils nur ein Los gewinnen, kommt das Verfahren nicht zur Anwendung. Wenn ein Bieter 2 Lose gewinnt erhält er den Zuschlag auf das Los, dass in seiner Wunschliste den höheren Platz hat. Der Gewinn des anderen Loses entfällt dann und es gewinnt das Los derjenige, der in dem Los auf Rang 2 ist. Sollte bei diesem Verfahren ein unwirtschaftliches Angebot den Zuschlag erhalten sollen, dann behält sich die Vergabestelle vor, die unwirtschaftlichen Lose aufzuheben und in einem Verhandlungsverfahren ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb neu auszuschreiben. _________________________________________________________________________________________________ Die Ausschreibung wird in folgende regionale Lose aufgeteilt: Los 1: Flensburg Glücksburg Los 2: Nordfriesland Schleswig-Flensburg Los 3: Rendsburg-Eckernförde Los 4: Pinneberg Steinburg Dithmarschen Los 5: Kiel Neumünster Lübeck _________________________________________________________________________________________________ Für diese Rahmenvereinbarung gelten die folgenden Höchstwerte für die zu erbringenden Leistungen im ausgeschriebenen Zeitraum: Los 1: 710.000,00 € netto. Los 2: 1.480.000,00 € netto. Los 3: 930.000,00 € netto. Los 4: 820.000,00 € netto. Los 5: 1.540.000,00 € netto. Mit Erreichen dieser Höchstwerte endet die Rahmenvereinbarung automatisch, unabhängig von der ursprünglich vereinbarten Laufzeit.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Machbarkeitsstudie Generalsanierung
description: Erstellung einer interdisziplinären Machbarkeitsstudie für die Generalsanierung der Bayerischen Staatsoper Nationaltheater Das Nationaltheater ist der Spielort der Bayerischen Staatsoper, des Bayerischen Staatsorchesters und des Bayerischen Staatsballetts. In seiner jetzigen neoklassizistischen Erscheinung wurde das Opernhaus im Jahr 1818 erstmals eröffnet. Fünf Jahre später wurde das Haus durch einen Brand zur Gänze zerstört und erneut aufgebaut. Der zweite Wiederaufbau nach der Zerstörung im Zweiten Weltkrieg bis auf die Außenmauern fand in den Jahren 1958 – 1963 statt. Seit der Wiedereröffnung im Jahr 1963 wurde keine Generalsanierung durchgeführt. Zum Gebäudekomplex gehört auch das Dekorationsmagazin entlang der Alfons-Goppel-Straße und das im Jahr 2003 fertiggestellte sog. „Neue Probengebäude“ am Marstallplatz. Weitere für den Probe- und Spielbetrieb genutzte Gebäude sind die Gebäude des Bayerischen Staatsballetts, Platzl 6 und 7, hierbei handelt es sich um ehemalige Corpsgebäude, die 1899 im Stil der Renaissance errichtet wurden. Mit zeitlichem Vorlauf und parallel zur Machbarkeitsstudie wird von Nutzerseite die Erstellung eines Bedarfsgesamtkonzepts einschließlich Visionsentwicklung („Oper der Zukunft“) beauftragt. Gleichzeitig wird außerdem die Bedarfsplanung für eine Interimslösung während der Generalsanierung des Nationaltheaters erstellt. Die Machbarkeitsuntersuchung soll in einem iterativen Prozess mit dem Nutzer und der Bedarfsplanung fortwährend abgeglichen werden. Die Beiträge und Ergebnisse aus der Machbarkeitsstudie sollen sodann in die Bedarfsplanung integriert werden und umgekehrt. Die Studie sollte sich mit den baulich- technischen Sanierungsnotwendigkeiten, funktionalen Optimierungen der betrieblichen Abläufe, möglichen Erweiterungsoptionen, den wesentlichen Belangen des Denkmalschutzes und, nicht zuletzt, den Möglichkeiten energetischer Optimierung der haustechnischen Anlagen auseinandersetzen. Bei der Erstellung der Machbarkeitsstudie sind insbesondere die Ziele des nachhaltigen Bauens zu verfolgen. Ein ganzheitlicher Ansatz ist vorzusehen um den gesamten Lebenszyklus der Gebäude unter Berücksichtigung der ökologischen, ökonomischen und soziokulturellen Qualität sowie der technischen und prozessualen Aspekte zu betrachten. Der Auftragsgegenstand beinhaltet die Erstellung einer Machbarkeitsstudie für die oben genannten Nutzungen in drei Varianten als Entscheidungsgrundlage für die in der Zukunft geplante Generalsanierung. Weitere Angaben sind der Aufgabenbeschreibung und den Vergabeunterlagen zu entnehmen.

title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – Generalplanungsleistungen für die Sanierung und Instandsetzung der Tiefgarage Hospitalstraße 6, 55232 Alzey
description: Die Stadt Alzey beabsichtigt die Vergabe von Generalplanungsleistungen für die Instandsetzung einer schadensbedingt sanierungsbedürftigen Tiefgarage in der Hospitalstraße 6, 55232 Alzey. Gegenstand der Maßnahme ist die Planung, Koordinierung, Ausschreibung, Vergabeunterstützung und objektüberwachende Begleitung der erforderlichen baulichen und technischen Sanierung sowie Instandsetzungsmaßnahmen. Grundlage der Planung sind die Ergebnisse des vorliegenden Untersuchungsberichts sowie die dort festgestellten Schadensbilder und Handlungsempfehlungen. Die Tiefgarage weist nach vorliegenden Untersuchungen erhebliche Schäden an den tragenden Stahlbetonbauteilen, an Bodenflächen, Rampen, Treppenhausanschlüssen sowie an technischen Einbauten auf. Als wesentliche Schadensursachen wurden chlorid- und carbonatisierungsinduzierte Bewehrungskorrosion, Undichtigkeiten, Rissbildungen, Hohllagen und Schäden an Oberflächen und Beschichtungen festgestellt; der Instandsetzungsbedarf ist kurzfristig gegeben. Ziel der zu vergebenen Leistung ist die Erarbeitung eines fachlich belastbaren, wirtschaftlichen und dauerhaft tragfähigen Instandsetzungskonzepts sowie die vollständige Planung und Begleitung der Umsetzung bis zur mängelfreien Fertigstellung. Die Instandsetzung ist so zu planen, dass die Tiefgarage nach Abschluss der Maßnahme wieder den Anforderungen an Standsicherheit, Dauerhaftigkeit, Verkehrssicherheit und Gebrauchstauglichkeit entspricht und eine weitere planmäßige Nutzungsdauer von 40 Jahren ermöglicht. Die Tiefgarage befindet sich im Nordwesten der Stadt Alzey und wird über die Hospitalstraße 6 erschlossen. Sie wurde im Jahr 1980 errichtet. Die Anlage besteht aus einem Bauteil, das nachträglich teilweise mit einem dreigeschossigen Wohn- und Geschäftshaus sowie einer Steinhalle überbaut wurde. Die verbleibenden Flächen oberhalb der Tiefgarage werden als zusätzliche Parkflächen genutzt. Insgesamt stehen rund 176 PKW-Stellplätze zur Verfügung, die sich auf zwei Parkgeschosse verteilen und öffentlich zugänglich sind.
